newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ivernia, Minorco get Lisheen planning permission.
newsitem.headline: Ivernia, Minorco get Lisheen planning permission.

text.p: Ivernia West Plc and Minorco Lisheen Limited, partners in the Lisheen mine joint venture, said on Tuesday that they had received final planning permission for the lead/zinc mine in the Irish midlands.
The Irish planning board, An Bord Pleanala, upheld an earlier decision by Tipperary county council to grant planning permission for the development of the mine, Ivernia said in a statement.
"This decision clears the way for the development at Lisheen of the largest base metal mine in Ireland in the past 20 years," it added.
The Lisheen mine, with planned annual outputs of 300,000 tonnes of zinc concentrates and 40,000 tonnes of lead concentrates, will rank as one of the top 10 world class zinc mines, Ivernia said.
Discussions are presently in progress with Ireland's energy department in connection with the granting of a state mining lease, the statement said.
Tenders are also being evaluated from leading international construction companies to build the mine and its associated milling facility.
Construction at the mine is expected to begin in July 1997 and commercial production of zinc and lead concentrates is planned for early 1999, Ivernia said.
